 With Brent crude crossing $110 per barrel, fuel prices have remained relatively stable over the past week. Petrol and diesel prices today: Petrol and diesel prices across major Indian cities remain largely unchanged on October 21 despite renewed pressure on global crude oil prices. Brent crude futures rose to over $110 per barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude climbed to more than $99 per barrel amid concerns over disruptions to oil supplies from West Asia. The attacks on vessels near the Strait of Hormuz and growing risks to shipping in the Red Sea have heightened concerns about the security of global energy supplies.
 Advertisement 
 The latest uptick in crude prices comes even as US President Donald Trump’s decision to waive certain restrictions linked to Russian energy supplies has raised hopes of additional fuel reaching the global market. However, continuing geopolitical tensions and threats to critical energy infrastructure could keep oil prices volatile.
 Read More
 For Indian consumers, petrol and diesel prices remain a key concern as India depends heavily on imported crude oil. State-run oil marketing companies, including Indian Oil Corporation, Bharat Petroleum and Hindustan Petroleum, have so far kept retail rates largely unchanged in major cities, leaving consumers exposed to potential future price pressures if international crude prices remain elevated.

 Global crude oil prices remain volatile on October 21 as markets assess the impact of potential changes in Russian fuel supplies and continuing disruptions to energy shipments through West Asia. While expectations of additional Russian supplies could help ease some pressure on the market, uncertainty surrounding key shipping routes and regional security continues to pose risks to global oil availability.
 For India, the sustained volatility in crude oil prices remains a concern for oil marketing companies (OMCs), as higher international crude and fuel costs can squeeze marketing margins when retail prices remain unchanged. State-run retailers Indian Oil Corporation, Bharat Petroleum and Hindustan Petroleum have so far maintained petrol and diesel prices across major cities. Any relief for these companies will depend on whether the cost of crude oil and refined petroleum products declines sufficiently and remains lower for a sustained period. For consumers, the immediate focus remains on whether changes in global oil markets will eventually lead to a revision in domestic fuel prices.

 What this means for you 
 Despite Brent crude at $110.4 per barrel, fuel prices have remained relatively stable over the past week. The rupee-dollar exchange rate is a key variable, given that India relies heavily on imported crude. When the rupee weakens against the dollar, the cost of procuring crude rises, which can feed directly into higher retail fuel prices.
 For daily commuters, this means no major shock at the pump, though prices remain elevated compared to previous years. Consumers should monitor local rates, as city-specific taxes vary even within the same state, leading to differences in retail fuel prices.
